identity.name: Dachepalli Publishers Limited
identity.industry: Education / Academic Publishing & Integrated School Solutions

summary.oneLiner: Dachepalli has transformed from a traditional textbook publisher into an integrated academic solutions platform, driven by in-house manufacturing of notebooks and uniforms, a scalable e-commerce platform (Pelican Edu Supply) tied to 150+ schools, and deep institutional partnerships — creating margin expansion, recurring revenue streams, and defensible market share growth in Tier 2/3 India.

one-line thesis: Dachepalli has transformed from a traditional textbook publisher into an integrated academic solutions platform, driven by in-house manufacturing of notebooks and uniforms, a scalable e-commerce platform (Pelican Edu Supply) tied to 150+ schools, and deep institutional partnerships — creating margin expansion, recurring revenue streams, and defensible market share growth in Tier 2/3 India.
financial scorecard: revenue: +42.2% YoY to INR 91.39cr; EBITDA: +78.6% YoY to INR 23.52cr, margin +524bps to 25.7% (no one-offs; margin expansion from paper cost decline + vertical integration); PAT (rptd): +81.8% YoY to INR 15.20cr; PAT (normalized): same (no distortions); order book: INR 70cr+ textbook orders (FY27), INR 60cr+ from Pelican platform (incl. uniforms); net debt: net cash position implied (no debt mentioned, capex funded internally)
guidance: revenue growth: INR 150cr+ (FY27), INR 220-230cr (FY28); margin: PAT 16-17% sustained, EBITDA to expand further with uniform scaling; order inflow: 100-150 new schools for Pelican platform; capex/commissioning: notebook capacity 10 tons/day (80% pre-booked), uniform stitching outsourced until 200-250 schools reached
order book & pipeline: INR 70cr+ from textbook business (FY27), INR 60cr+ from Pelican platform (textbooks, notebooks, stationery, uniforms) across 150 schools
segment / subsidiary detail: Textbook: INR 70cr revenue (FY26), 10,000 schools across 15 states; Pelican E-commerce: INR 20cr revenue (FY26), 50 schools, 70% Dachepalli textbooks + 30% third-party + notebooks/stationery; Notebooks: in-house manufacturing launched (10 tons/day capacity); Uniforms: pilot in 3 schools, scaling to 50 existing Pelican schools in FY27; Stationery: not yet manufactured, white-label currently, target 30k units to trigger in-house production
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into 28 states + 8 UTs (from 15); stationery manufacturing (pens, geometry boxes) at 30k unit volume; curriculum licensing (e.g., The Money Tree); potential LMS platform monetization; international school exports (long-term)
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 25.7% (FY26) driven by: 1) 40-50% paper cost decline since 2020 (INR 120/kg → INR 65/kg); 2) in-house printing (75% utilization); 3) notebook manufacturing replacing third-party purchases (higher margin); 4) uniform margins ~50% EBITDA (scaling to 50 schools in FY27); 5) Pelican platform reduces distribution cost
capex / expansion: INR 15-20cr invested in notebook manufacturing machinery; warehouse expansion (1.5L sq ft owned); printing capacity scaled to handle INR 250cr revenue; uniform stitching outsourced until scale threshold (200-250 schools)
capital allocation: Funds from IPO used to hire sales teams, enter 4 new states (UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam), and fund in-house capex (notebooks, printing); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; reinvestment prioritized over payout
risks & watch-items: 1) Regulatory scrutiny on school supply chain profit margins; 2) delayed school payments (200+ days debtor days due to academic cycle mismatch); 3) competition from Navneet/S. Chand entering e-commerce; 4) uniform supply chain complexity; 5) over-reliance on state board academic cycles
management quality / tone: Highly confident, visionary, and execution-focused; management explicitly rejects traditional publishing model; emphasizes institutional stickiness, vertical integration, and platform scalability; acknowledges challenges (e.g., uniform logistics) but frames them as solvable with scale; targets INR 500cr+ revenue by FY29
non-obvious takeaways: 1) 200+ day debtor days are an accounting artifact — cash collection aligns with school reopening (June), not invoice date; 2) Pelican platform’s 50% textbook requirement is a stealth channel control mechanism — not just a sales channel but a school adoption tool; 3) ‘6 brands’ strategy is a market segmentation tactic to bypass school procurement rules that limit single-vendor adoption; 4) paper cost decline is structural — digital substitution in non-textbook paper use has permanently lowered input costs

scorecard.pe_basis: TTM trailing (spec band written for forward P/E)
